title: First Unique Character in a String
statement: Given a string `s`, find the first non-repeating character in it and return its index. If it does not exist, return `-1`.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

The character 'v' is the first non-repeating character at index 2.

editorial.approach: Build a frequency hash map of all characters. Then scan the string from left to right, checking the frequency of each character. Return index of the first character with frequency === 1.

hints: You can keep track of character frequencies using a map or an array of size 26.
Iterate through the string once to count how many times each character appears.
Iterate through the string a second time and check the count of each character. Return the index of the first one with a count of 1.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: For each character at index `i`, check if it exists elsewhere in the string using `.indexOf` and `.lastIndexOf`.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Store frequency counts in an array of size 26 (since string only contains lowercase letters). Scan string twice to find the first character with count === 1 in O(n) time.
optimizedSolution.spaceComplexity: O(1) (since the size of the alphabet is constant, 26)

interviewExplanation: A brute-force index lookup takes O(n^2) time. We optimize it by using an alphabet-sized array to store counts, running in O(n) time. The space complexity remains O(1) as the array size is fixed at 26 characters.
